status.coach: decided by the coach (docs/decisions.md); source support noted
status.proposed: Claude's proposal, NOT yet decided by the coach
status.open: source not read yet or value missing: shown in the app as 'OPEN – to confirm'

ROTHSCHILD2025.read: abstract; likely (not verified) the basis of Intervals.icu's ROTHSCHILD_2024 setting

ETTEMA2009.cite: Ettema G, Lorås HW. Efficiency in cycling: a review. Eur J Appl Physiol. 2009;106(1):1–14.

CHO-DUR-01.title: Ride ≤ 30 min: no carbohydrate needed during
CHO-DUR-01.use: duration ≤ 30 min → 0 g/h; Jeukendrup Fig. 1 starts at 30 min (nothing advised below)

CHO-DUR-02.title: 30–75 min: small amounts or mouth rinse
CHO-DUR-02.use: target 0 g/h. Jeukendrup 2014 / Thomas 2016 also mention a mouth rinse; coach decision G1 (24-11-2026): the app does not advise mouth rinses

CHO-DUR-03.title: 75 min–2 h: 30–60 g/h (low for easy, up to 60 for key/race)
CHO-DUR-03.use: Q8. Jeukendrup Fig. 1: 1–2 h 30 g/h; Thomas 2016 Table 2: 1–2,5 h 30–60 g/h (read). Band starts at 75 min, where both 45–75 min bands end

CHO-DUR-04.title: 2–2,5 h: up to 60 g/h
CHO-DUR-04.use: Q8. Jeukendrup Fig. 1: 2–3 h 60 g/h, single or multiple transportable carbohydrates. Range low end = previous band

CHO-DUR-05.title: > 2,5 h: up to 90 g/h, only multiple transportable carbohydrates
CHO-DUR-05.use: Jeukendrup Fig. 1: > 2,5 h 90 g/h ONLY multiple transportable carbohydrates; for well-trained athletes, aspiring athletes may adjust downwards

CHO-EASY-01.title: Easy endurance/recovery ride ≤ 2 h: carbohydrate optional (0–30 g/h), default 0
CHO-EASY-01.use: Q7. Applies only in the 75 min–2 h band (≤ 75 min is already 0 g/h) and only when INT-LOW-01 says the ride is low intensity. Impey 2018 proposes no CHO for steady sessions below lactate threshold (hypothesis); Jeukendrup 2014: lower absolute intensity → adjust downwards

CHO-SHORT-01.title: Key/race 45–75 min: optional 30–60 g/h, athlete's choice
CHO-SHORT-01.use: cases 02–04 review H1: sources say 'small amounts' for 45–75 min; coach rule: optional 30–60 g/h, default shown 30 g/h, athlete may choose up to 60 g/h or nothing

INT-LOW-01.title: Low intensity = IF ≤ top of Z2 and no hard time
INT-LOW-01.use: review R6: IF ≤ athlete's Z2 upper bound / 100 and 0 s above INT-HARD-01

INT-HARD-01.title: Hard effort = step's lower bound above top of Z3
INT-HARD-01.use: review R6: a step is hard when its lower target is above the athlete's Z3 upper bound (90 % FTP with your zones). Used by TIME-03 and GOAL-01

GOAL-01.title: Goal suggestion without a tag
GOAL-01.use: review R6: tag wins (race/key/endurance/recovery); without a tag: 'key' if the ride has hard time, else 'endurance'; the athlete can change it

CHO-INT-01.title: Lower absolute intensity → carbohydrate advice may be adjusted downwards
CHO-INT-01.use: qualitative support for CHO-EASY-01 and for the low end of CHO-DUR-03; no numeric factor in the source

CHO-MTC-01.title: Glucose-only carbohydrate ≤ 60 g/h
CHO-MTC-01.use: matcher: carbohydrate from glucose/maltodextrin-only items (or unknown type) ≤ 60 g/h; above that it must come from glucose+fructose items

CHO-MTC-02.title: Glucose:fructose 1:0,8 preferred, 2:1 accepted
CHO-MTC-02.use: informational in the 'why' text; not a hard constraint (both ratios are mixes)

CHO-CAP-01.title: Guideline maximum 90 g/h
CHO-CAP-01.use: Q6. No target above 90 g/h unless CHO-CAP-02

CHO-CAP-02.title: Athlete cap up to 120 g/h only if gut-trained
CHO-CAP-02.use: Q6. Podlogar & Wallis: evidence for > 90 g/h inconclusive → shown with low confidence

CHO-GUT-01.title: Target = min(guideline, athlete tolerance); advise gut training when tolerance is lower
CHO-GUT-01.use: brief + Jeukendrup 2017 (practise high intake in training; no protocol numbers). Podlogar & Wallis: improved absorption not yet established

TIME-01.title: First intake in the first 15–20 min
TIME-01.use: brief; first slot at 15 min when the ride has a carbohydrate target

TIME-02.title: Spread intake every 15–20 min
TIME-02.use: brief; Kerksick 2017 abstract: fluid-carbohydrate every 10–15 min. Slots every 20 min

TIME-03.title: No intake planned inside hard efforts
TIME-03.use: brief + cases 02–04 ('eat/drink in the recovery intervals'): hard efforts separated by < 2 min (proposal) form one set; a slot inside a set moves to just before it, or into the recovery after it

TIME-06.title: Sustained hard effort > 20 min: intake allowed inside it, gels/drink only
TIME-06.use: case 09 review I3: a hard block (after TIME-03 merging) longer than 20 min is a sustained effort (time trial, race pace); slots stay every 20 min inside it and are never easy, so TIME-04 keeps solids out. Shorter hard blocks keep TIME-03

TIME-04.title: Solid food only in easy parts
TIME-04.use: brief; solids only in slots where the 5 min around them stay ≤ Z2 upper bound; gels/drink otherwise

TIME-05.title: First intake by 15–20 min wins over 'solids only in easy parts'
TIME-05.use: review R2: first serving = gel/drink if in stock; with only solid food it goes at the first slot when that moment itself is ≤ top of Z2 (the last easy moment before the hard block)

FLU-01.title: Starting fluid range 0,4–0,8 l/h (sweat rate unknown)
FLU-01.use: Thomas 2016: the fluid plan for most athletes typically achieves 0,4–0,8 l/h (citing Sawka 2007), customised to tolerance. Sawka 2007: 0,4–0,8 l/h ad libitum is a starting point (marathon data), higher for heavier athletes in warm weather, lower for lighter athletes in the cool; individual plans from body-weight changes. Default = mid-range

FLU-02.title: Avoid > 2 % body-mass loss
FLU-02.use: Sawka 2007 (full text): drinking aims to prevent > 2 % body-weight loss from water deficit; > 2 % can degrade aerobic performance, especially in warm-hot weather (evidence category A). Used in FLU-04

FLU-03.title: Never plan to drink more than sweat loss (hyponatraemia)
FLU-03.use: Thomas 2016: over-drinking in excess of sweat and urine losses is the primary cause of hyponatraemia; neither drink in excess of sweat rate nor let dehydration reach problematic levels. Sawka 2007: fluid consumption that exceeds sweating rate is the primary factor in exercise-associated hyponatraemia (category A). Fluid target ≤ known sweat rate

FLU-04.title: Known sweat rate: drink sweat rate minus the 2 % allowance, never more than sweat rate
FLU-04.use: proposal: fluid l/h = sweat rate − (2 % × body mass) / ride hours, between 0 and sweat rate. Sawka 2007: 1 ml sweat ≈ 1 g body mass; correct the weigh test for drinks and urine

FLU-05.title: No temperature bands: heat is handled with an individual sweat test
FLU-05.use: McCubbin 2020: a simple definition of heat stress is not possible (temperature, humidity, wind, sun, clothing and activity together); sweat rate 150–3500 ml/h between athletes. No bands applied; with a forecast temperature the app advises a sweat-rate test in similar conditions (review R4)

FLU-06.title: Indoor: no fixed adjustment; use a fan and a sweat-rate test indoors
FLU-06.use: McCubbin 2020: airflow changes heat loss and sweat sodium, but no numeric factor is given. No adjustment applied; advice: fan + sweat-rate test on the trainer

NA-01.title: Drink sodium 20–30 mmol/l (≈ 460–690 mg per litre) for rides > 1 h
NA-01.use: Sawka 2007 (replaces Convertino 1996): sports drinks for prolonged activity ~20–30 meq/l sodium (Institute of Medicine), i.e. 460–690 mg/l. Convertino 1996 gave 0,5–0,7 g/l. Sodium mg/h = fluid l/h × mg/l

NA-02.title: Upper end for salty sweaters, sweat rate > 1,2 l/h or rides > 2 h
NA-02.use: Thomas 2016: sodium should be taken when sweat sodium losses are large: sweat rate > 1,2 l/h, salty sweat, or exercise > 2 h. Heat threshold still OPEN (McCubbin)

NA-03.title: No sodium target for rides ≤ 60 min
NA-03.use: review R1: water only; NA-01 applies above 60 min

PRE-01.title: Pre-ride 1–4 g carbohydrate/kg, 1–4 h before (rides > 60 min)
PRE-01.use: Thomas 2016 Table 2: pre-event fuelling before exercise > 60 min, 1–4 g/kg consumed 1–4 h before; low fat/fibre/protein. Rides ≤ 60 min: normal meal. Case 05 review D3 (coach): only races get the full 1–4 g/kg; key/endurance/recovery = normal breakfast with carbohydrate, about 1 g/kg

PRE-02.title: Pre-ride fluid 5–10 ml/kg in the 2–4 h before
PRE-02.use: Thomas 2016: 5–10 ml/kg body weight in the 2–4 h before exercise, urine pale yellow. Sawka 2007: ~5–7 ml/kg at least 4 h before, another ~3–5 ml/kg about 2 h before if no urine or dark urine; salty snacks help retain it

CAF-01.title: Caffeine 3–6 mg/kg about 60 min before
CAF-01.use: Guest 2021. Engine uses the low end, 3 mg/kg (proposal)

CAF-02.title: Low dose 1–3 mg/kg later in long rides
CAF-02.use: Guest 2021: low doses mid/late in exercise beneficial; minimal effective dose may be ~2 mg/kg. Engine: 2 mg/kg at 2/3 of rides > 2,5 h (proposal)

CAF-03.title: Caffeine planned only for races; optional for key sessions
CAF-03.use: case 05 review D2 (replaces R5): race → planned; key → shown as optional; never when the athlete's caffeine use is 'none'

CAF-05.title: EFSA: single dose ≤ 200 mg, ≤ 400 mg per day from all sources
CAF-05.use: EFSA 2015: single doses up to 200 mg (about 3 mg/kg for 70 kg) are of no concern for healthy adults, also < 2 h before intense exercise; habitual intake up to 400 mg/day from all sources (about 5,7 mg/kg); 100 mg may disturb sleep close to bedtime. Engine: every planned dose ≤ 200 mg, planned doses together ≤ 400 mg, with a note that coffee counts too

CAF-07.title: No planned caffeine during pregnancy
CAF-07.use: EFSA 2015: single doses of no concern for non-pregnant adults do not apply to pregnant women before intense exercise (no studies). Health flag pregnancy → no caffeine planned

CAF-06.title: Bedtime cut-off
CAF-06.use: Guest 2021: half-life about 4–6 h, caffeine before bed may disturb sleep, no hours given. Proposal: no dose later than 6 h before bedtime

REC-01.title: Next session < 8 h: 1,0–1,2 g carbohydrate/kg/h for 4 h + ~0,3 g protein/kg
REC-01.use: Thomas 2016 Table 2: speedy refuelling, < 8 h between two fuel-demanding sessions, 1–1,2 g/kg/h for the first 4 h; protein 0,25–0,3 g/kg in the first 2 h. Podlogar & Wallis agree

REC-03.title: Rehydrate 125–150 % of the fluid deficit
REC-03.use: Thomas 2016: 1,25–1,5 l fluid for every 1 kg lost, with sodium. Sawka 2007: ~1,5 l per kg for rapid recovery, spread over time, with sodium. Always shown (case 06 review C5); exact ml when the sweat rate is known (deficit = (sweat rate − planned fluid) × hours), else 'weigh before and after'

REC-02.title: Otherwise: meal with carbohydrate + 0,25–0,40 g protein/kg within 2 h
REC-02.use: Kerksick 2017 abstract: 20–40 g (0,25–0,40 g/kg) protein, immediately to 2 h after

REC-04.title: Recovery ride ≤ 60 min: only drink water afterwards
REC-04.use: case 01 review F1: no protein advice after a short recovery ride (the sources aim protein at demanding sessions); water only

EE-01.title: Energy expenditure: kJ of work ≈ kcal (gross efficiency 20–25 %)
EE-01.use: information only. kcal = kJ ÷ (GE × 4,184). Ettema & Lorås 2009: realistic gross efficiency in cycling is about 20–25 %; it rises with work rate and levels off above ~150 W; delta efficiency ~24 % (SD 2,6). So 1 kJ of work ≈ 0,96–1,20 kcal

MATCH-01.title: Carbohydrate within ± 10 % of target; at most 3 product types besides drinks
MATCH-01.use: ± 10 % from the brief; max 3 product types is a proposal (search limit)

MATCH-02.title: Tie-breakers: within ± 5 % first, then fewest items, favourites, closest to target, product ID
MATCH-02.use: brief; fixed order so the same input always gives the same plan. Case 08 review I1: inside ± 10 %, plans within ± 5 % of the target come first (2 bottles + 4 gels = 450 g beats 2 bottles + 3 gels = 405 g)

MATCH-05.title: Very concentrated bottles at most half of the bottles; the rest water
MATCH-05.use: case 08 review I1: bottles above MATCH-03 (80 g/l) are at most half of the bottles (at least 1), so there is water to drink with them; more carbohydrate then comes from gels/food

HEAT-01.title: Cool or cold drinks in the heat
HEAT-01.use: McCubbin 2020: drinks < 22 °C increase palatability and intake; cold (< 10 °C) or iced drinks may help in hot conditions. Advice text shown from the HEAT-02 hot-day temperature (25 °C), coach decision T7 25-11-2026

HEAT-02.title: Hot day (≥ 25 °C), sweat rate unknown: 750 ml/h
HEAT-02.use: case 07 review E1: coach rule; stays inside the sourced 0,4–0,8 l/h (Thomas 2016). Sodium follows the fluid. Sweat-test advice asked once in the profile, not per ride

MATCH-03.title: Prefer bottles ≤ 80 g/l (8 %); above that warn 'drink water with it'
MATCH-03.use: review R3, raised to 120 g/l in case 06 review C6. Drinks are always mixed at label strength (C6). Convertino 1996: solutions > 10 % (100 g/l) can draw water into the gut – shown in the warning. Sawka 2007: when one drink must cover both fluid and carbohydrate, ≤ 8 % (80 g/l) – coach lowered the limit from 120 to 80 g/l (case 08 review I4)

MATCH-04.title: The athlete chooses between plans: with drink, or gels/food only
MATCH-04.use: case 06 review C6 + case 07 review E3: the matcher returns the best drink-only, drink + food and without-drink plans; the drink + food plan is shown first when it fits ± 10 %

AGE-01.title: Under 18 when ride year − birth year ≤ 18
AGE-01.use: only the birth year is stored, so an 18-year-old born late in the year is treated as under 18 (safe side)

MAN-01.title: Ride without blocks, endurance: one steady step in Z2
MAN-01.use: Phase 2 P1, confirmed by the coach 25-11-2026 for endurance rides. Only timing and the intensity checks use it; carbohydrate follows the duration band

MAN-02.title: Ride without blocks, recovery: one steady step in Z1
MAN-02.use: Phase 2 P1, Claude proposal; not yet answered by the coach

MAN-03.title: Ride without blocks, key session or race: intensity not known
MAN-03.use: Phase 2 P1: left OPEN by the coach 25-11-2026 (to-do). Until decided the app calculates with one steady step in Z4 and shows the result as OPEN – to confirm

METH-IF.title: Intensity factor from planned steps (30-s rolling, 4th-power mean)
METH-IF.use: normalised-power method applied to the planned steps; method choice, no nutrition value
